body: @jridgewell can you summarize why this strategy for streaming is ideal/optimal for our documentation? Can be bullets too. It's a killer optimization you're adding that is not intuitive
author: jaredpalmer

body:
The is mostly to use the `pull`/`transform` method in `ReadableStream`/`TransformStream`. The old way of using `for await (… of stream)` is eager, meaning we're always trying to process more data and push it into the client stream. But, the client may not need any more data, they may be busy doing their own work with our last chunk.

By switching to `pull`/`transform`, we're able to give control to the consumer. If the consumer doesn't need data, we won't be processing anything. If they do, then `pull`/`transform` will be continually called until a new chunk of data is emitted by our `EventSourceParser`.

I decided not to combine the 2 `TransformerStreams` so that the callback-and-encoding code could be shared between each AI model. They're all doing the exact same thing.

body:
> 2 APIs for this instead of this `mode` stuff: `OpenAITextStream` and `OpenAIDataStream`

Makes sense, agree that's probably easier. Will update.

EDIT: A call to `OpenAIStream(res, { mode: "raw" })` is actually analogous to just `AIStream(res)`, so we don't even need to do that. Apparently it's redundant to wrap with `AIStream()` at all if you have a ReadableStream already, just return new `Response(res)`.

There will ultimately end up being more modes than just raw/text though.
author: ctjlewis

body:
@jaredpalmer I added completion JSON parsing to demonstrate, and converted this to a draft for now. 

The mode is just a way to switch between chunk parsers. You can see how this pattern lets you do `OpenAIStream(res, { mode: "json" })` or wrap whatever you want with `AIStream(res, { mode, parsers: ... })`. This can easily be extended to better integration with [OpenAI Function Calling](https://openai.com/blog/function-calling-and-other-api-updates) or JSON-like prompt responses.

body:
> > It would be nice to parse the response from OpenAI differently, when it comes to function calling. Since it won't be a stream response. 🤔
> 
> Function calling responses are streamable too. Furthermore, especially if the `function_call` parameter is set to `auto` in the request, you don't know whether or not the model will decide to call a function, so the streaming utils must be updated to support streaming the function calls to the clients as well.

I mean, don't get my wrong, it's nice that we could stream function call responses, but I guess if we do that, we could break the SRP (Single-responsibility principle).

Consider this, for example, the Open API payload endpoint, accepts an `stream`  parameter which is boolean. 
If this parameter is false, we may don't want to parse the response as `stream`, We can stop that logic at that moment, and parse the response differently. We can also add support to useChat or any other interface for the user to choose when they would like streamed responses or not. In my head, this new function calling functionality is 3 additional steps in the middle of the flow. That is:

- Seeing if finish_reason is 'function_call' ( 99,99% yes, depending on your software design)
- Call your function
- Call again the API with the function results with role='function'

Then, resume the streaming flow. 
But, I may be wrong in my point of view, anyways, I'm trying to reason about it, together.

If you look at my [comment explaining how function calling chunks are streamed](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ai/pull/178/files#diff-b4fc3cf85f3dc974899314160d4930248499e7e5c371f123d4d9a4948c6b3e62R14) or my [test data showing the chunks](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ai/pull/178/files#diff-c386744b666862eb2649d1936a536bc75686a61b0d5a4d9c243a303fd765907fR64), you can see that the function call name is not at risk of being malformed, but the function call "arguments" can be malformed JSON (or improperly escaped), so my PR leaves the arguments as a string, and leaves it to the client to handle the case where OpenAI returns malformed JSON in the arguments.

body:
Take https://github.com/vercel-labs/ai/issues/205#issuecomment-1603437504 as an example. Let's say we wanted to stream both the responses.

in first chain

```
Tragedy at Sunset on the Beach is a story of love, loss, and redemption. It follows the story of two young lovers, Jack and Jill, who meet on a beach at sunset. They quickly fall in love and plan to spend the rest of their lives together. \n\nHowever, tragedy strikes when Jack is killed in a car accident. Jill is left devastated and unable to cope with the loss of her beloved. She spirals into a deep depression and begins to lose hope. \n\nJust when all seems lost, Jill discovers that Jack had left her a letter before his death. In the letter, he tells her that he will always love her and that she should never give up hope. With this newfound strength, Jill is able to find the courage to move on with her life and find happiness again. \n\nTragedy at Sunset on the Beach is a story of love, loss, and redemption. It is a story of hope and courage in the face of tragedy. It is a story of finding strength in the darkest of times and of never giving up.",     
```

handleChainEnd gets called, stream is closed. Second chain can't write the second response

```
Tragedy at Sunset on the Beach is a powerful and moving story of love, loss, and redemption. The play follows the story of two young lovers, Jack and Jill, whose plans for a future together are tragically cut short when Jack is killed in a car accident. \n\nThe play is beautifully written and the performances are outstanding. The actors bring a depth of emotion to their characters that is both heartbreaking and inspiring. The story is full of unexpected twists and turns, and the audience is taken on an emotional rollercoaster as Jill struggles to come to terms with her loss. \n\nThe play is ultimately a story of hope and resilience, and it is sure to leave audiences with a newfound appreciation for life and love. Tragedy at Sunset on the Beach is a must-see for anyone looking for an emotionally charged and thought-provoking experience."
```

There's probably many ways to fix this, but the way I suggested in this PR seems to work for most use cases I've tried.

body:
Thanks for the work on this. I'm going to try out function calling and so may not need to stream extra data.

However I've been thinking about DX and have an idea: I think the core data of RAG apps is not a _message_ log, it's an _event_ log containing user messages, function calls, function responses, and assistant messages. A RAG app needs to present views of that event log to both the user and the assistant; the assistant's view is a message log, and the user's view is whatever JSON drives their UI. The current API (pre-experimental_streamData), which thinks of things as OpenAI-style message logs rather than generic event logs, makes it hard to handle those two different views of the data.

For example, in my RAG app I want my search results to be formatted as a plaintext system message for the OpenAI message array, but want to view those same results as JSON client side, so that I can present a "related research" UI section. Under the current functionCalling API that might involve parsing system messages client side, which is unwieldy. With the current streamData API that would involve interleaving the data array back into my message history as system messages, which is also a bit awkward. Either that or duplicating data as system messages AND streamData.

So I think my ideal API would be to have a generic type called "event" that looks something like this:
```typescript
type Event<T> = {
  name: string // or generic string literal
  data: T
}
```
This `Event` type would be part of message history, and I would set up functions on client and server side to determine how to map that event to a system message for OpenAI, and how to interpret the event data as UI client side.

This is a bit different from message-correlated data, since the data event is a neighboring member in the message/event array rather than an additional field of a message. I think that's more sensible, since fundamentally the data event has its own chronological place in the stream, you can even think of a data event as a message from a 3rd party agent, like a 'search agent' who just sent a message to the stream.

Curious to hear people's thoughts on this!

body:
@peterdresslar Can you provide an example? Steps I used to reproduce (and fix) the error locally: 1. Clone https://github.com/ctate/vercel-ai (my fork) 2. Checkout the `issue-567` branch via `git checkout issue-567` 3. Run `pnpm install && pnpm run build` 4. Run the "next-openai" example: `pnpm --filter=next-openai run dev` 5. Add some debugging code in `examples/next-openai/app/page.tsx` like `{error &&
{error.message}
}` Then, to test, I simply opened localhost:3000, turned wifi off, asked a question, and saw the error. Then I turned wifi back on and asked another question. The error disappeared and I got a result back. (before the fix, the error never went away) The event loop for handleSubmit is `handleSubmit()` > `append()` > `triggerRequest()`. `triggerRequest()` is also called via `reload()`. In both scenarios, `triggerRequest()` seems like a good place to clear the error because `triggerRequest()` is also the only place where an error is set (it's also the same function that changes the `isLoading` state). Lmk if this helps. Thanks!

`useAssistant` is on the client side. The goal is that all assistant based-behavior can run on the server side, without any client involvement. The client is only notified with information that could lead to rendering changes (e.g. progress information, streaming messages in the future, etc.)

Can you point to the exact while loop? Please note that a) the server side implementation is an example, any production system would use something way more complex to guarantee resiliency, failover, etc., and b) most of the code has async calls.

I see. Does anyone know if there is a way to return the function call decision to the? In the example, the model in the backend has access to the function call and function call return stuff but the frontend doesn't have access to it. Basically i'd like the frontend to know what function have been called and what is it's return value.

Line 97-104 of this [file](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/5f4115bdbba7a7fcaae15879b421a41b20620c2c/examples/next-openai/app/api/chat-with-tools/route.ts#L97)
author: frmsaul

body:
You can return a string from the function call on the server and that will get sent to the client as a standard message.  So you could do something like 
```javascript
      return JSON.stringify({function: toolCall.func.name, result: 'Handled'});
```
And then look for json formatted messages in the client.

If you want to return a function response to the API, (like the current weather) for the model to interpret and also tell the client that the function was handled, you might be able to get clever by adding some sort of `modelGotFunctionReturn` function on the client side where you tell the model to tell you about functions that were handled.  Not sure if that would work, but might be worth a try.

If none of that works, you could look into
https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/5f4115bdbba7a7fcaae15879b421a41b20620c2c/packages/core/streams/openai-stream.ts#L673
and see if there is some changes you could make to add the functionality you are looking for.

I've been away from this code for a bit so I don't have too much more to offer than that.  Although, there is a draft PR up with some changes to that code that you could also look into for handing some calls on the server and others on the client.
https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/1123

As per the OpenAI API docs, there should be a `JSON.parse(tool.function.arguments)` I actually ran into this in a different project I was working on so I did a ` if typeof arguments === "string" ? body:
Thanks sm for working on this.

When you say "parallel client/server tool calls", would it also support one either: (1) allowing a server-side tool call to call a client-side tool, or (2) passing the result of a server-side tool to the client?

I've been trying to find a workable impl for either of the two above scenarios, but the closest thing I've seen is serializing the result of server-side tool calls via JSON and sending it back as an assistant message, which comes w/ its own set of caveats like the lack of a follow-up message from the assistant w/o an additional user message.
author: rajdtta

body:
> When you say "parallel client/server tool calls", would it also support one either: (1) allowing a server-side tool call to call a client-side tool, or (2) passing the result of a server-side tool to the client?

It will support both client and server side tool calls, and they can be mixed and parallel.

### Example

You define 2 tools, one that is executed client side (i.e. has no execute method), and one that is executed server-side (i.e. with an execute method). The client side code then receives 3 related events:

- tool call for client side tool
- tool call for server side tool
- tool result for server side tool

On the client, you'd execute the client-side tool, do whatever you want with the server side tool result, and then use onFinish to send back both tool results to the server, so that the AI can continue the conversation (this is important for this to work at all, because OpenAI expects tool results for all tool calls it invokes). 

On the next roundtrip, the LLM will know the tool results and can come up with text responses or more tool calls.

Please note that this is a WIP and the design might change.

And the way we handle the 2nd invocation flow is now when the `Message` that's passed to `onFinish` contains `toolInvocation` results, we call `experimental_addToolResult`, for both client and server tools?
> 
> How do we send back the tool results to the LLM in the server-side tool case without direct access to `triggerRequest` - or does `experimental_addToolResult` handle de-duplicating the `toolInvocation` results array and we can do something like this:
> 
> ```
>   // handle sending response of server-side tool back to LLM
>   
>   const { experimental_addToolResult } = useChat({
>     ....
>     onFinish: async (message) => {
>       if (
>         message.role === 'assistant' &&
>         message.toolInvocations &&
>         message.toolInvocations.every(
>           (toolInvocation) => 'result' in toolInvocation,
>         )
>       ) {
>         return message.toolInvocations.forEach((toolInvocation) => {
>           if ('result' in toolInvocation) {
>             experimental_addToolResult({
>               result: toolInvocation.result,
>               toolCallId: toolInvocation.toolCallId,
>             })
>           }
>         })
>       }
> 
>       return onFinish(message)
>     },
>   ...
>   })
> ```

From my understanding, `experimental_addToolResult` is used to pipe back results from client tool invocations back to the LLM (so that it's able to interpret the results and use it to decide its next step).

As for having the LLM interpret server-side tool calls, that's something I'm still trying to figure out in my sandbox. Quickly subbing in the snippet you sent above just causes the model to repeatedly call the server tool in a loop, and trying to use `append` to add a user message makes the model trigger a duplicate tool call (but interestingly, the result of the duplicate/second tool call doesn't get appended to the toolInvocation object despite it executing on the server-side).
